examples.question_text: Rewrite each ratio using its complementary co-ratio: (a) $\sec 32^{\circ}$, (b) $\cot 63^{\circ}$, (c) $\operatorname{cosec} 24^{\circ}$.

Simplify without using a calculator: (a) $\dfrac{\cot29^{\circ}+\tan61^{\circ}}{\cot29^{\circ}}$, (b) $\sec(90^{\circ}-\alpha)\sin\alpha$, (c) $\dfrac{\tan(90^{\circ}-\alpha)}{\cot(90^{\circ}-\alpha)}$, where $\alpha$ is acute.
For acute $\alpha$, prove (a) $\operatorname{cosec}(90^{\circ}-\alpha)=\sec\alpha$ and (b) $\tan(90^{\circ}-\alpha)=\cot\alpha$, using sine and cosine complementary identities.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\operatorname{cosec}(90^{\circ}-\alpha)\\&=\frac{1}{\sin(90^{\circ}-\alpha)}\\&=\frac{1}{\cos\alpha}\\&=\sec\alpha\\&=\mathrm{RHS}\end{aligned}$

(b)
$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\tan(90^{\circ}-\alpha)\\&=\frac{\sin(90^{\circ}-\alpha)}{\cos(90^{\circ}-\alpha)}\\&=\frac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\\&=\cot\alpha\\&=\mathrm{RHS}\end{aligned}$

Since $\alpha$ is acute, the denominators are nonzero.

examples.question_text:
(a) Find $t$ if $\cot(2t+8^{\circ})=\tan(3t+7^{\circ})$, where both arguments are acute.

(b) Find $k$ if $\sec(24^{\circ}-k)=\operatorname{cosec}(2k+42^{\circ})$, where $0^{\circ}\leq24^{\circ}-k<90^{\circ}$ and $0^{\circ}<2k+42^{\circ}\leq90^{\circ}$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Equal co-ratios of acute angles have complementary arguments.

$\begin{aligned}(2t+8^{\circ})+(3t+7^{\circ})&=90^{\circ}\\5t+15^{\circ}&=90^{\circ}\\5t&=75^{\circ}\\t&=15^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The arguments are $38^{\circ}$ and $52^{\circ}$; both are acute.

(b) Secant on $[0^{\circ},90^{\circ})$ is one-to-one, and $\operatorname{cosec}B=\sec(90^{\circ}-B)$ on the stated interval.

$\begin{aligned}(24^{\circ}-k)+(2k+42^{\circ})&=90^{\circ}\\k+66^{\circ}&=90^{\circ}\\k&=24^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The arguments are $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$. They satisfy the restrictions, and $\sec0^{\circ}=\operatorname{cosec}90^{\circ}=1$.

Use $\cos u=\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-u\right)$.

$\begin{aligned}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}-x\right)&=\sin x\end{aligned}$

For the given domain, $\dfrac{\pi}{3}-x\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{6},\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$ and $x\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Sine is one-to-one on $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, so the arguments are equal.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi}{3}-x&=x\\2x&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\x&=\frac{\pi}{6}\end{aligned}$

This lies in the domain and gives $\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac12$.
